Why README lagged. The release PR touches 12 files and README is not one of them, so What’s New is structurally one release behind every time. The refresh step in release-please.yml is continue-on-error: true, so a miss degrades to a warning nobody reads. This PR runs the stamper; the durable fix is a separate question.

Two remaining hits are correct. changelog-data.ts holds historical entries naming the old skill, and a transient semgrep log mentions it. Historical prose must not be rewritten to look current — that is the documented exemption in the skill-authoring rule.

The About page derives, it does not hardcode

app/(home)/about/page.tsx
   └─ imports COUNTS, SITE from lib/constants.ts
        ├─ version  ← manifests/ork.json
        └─ COUNTS   ← generated/shared-data.ts (TOTALS)

Nothing on the About page or in BANNER_TEXT needed editing for this release. Both follow the manifest and the generated totals, so a version bump propagates on rebuild rather than requiring a hand edit that could rot.

Incidental fix: a file mode that was silently wrong

tests/skills/structure/
  test-agent-no-version-snapshot.mjs   100755   ← sibling
  test-targets-floor-agreement.mjs     100644   ← wrong
  test-upstream-version-drift.mjs      100755   ← sibling
  • The file carries a #!/usr/bin/env node shebang.
  • npm run build chmods it to 755 on every run, so it appeared dirty after any build and was easy to stage by accident.
  • 755 is correct; it was committed 644 and the build has been quietly correcting it in the working tree ever since. Now committed at the right mode.
